title: Images of smooth pointed curves through a fixed point are dense
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be a smooth separated geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x_0\in X(k)$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. There exist a set $I$, smooth separated geometrically integral finite-type curves $C_i/k$ of dimension one [def-sc-curves, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], points $c_i\in C_i(k)$, and $k$-morphisms $u_i:C_i\to X$ with $u_i(c_i)=x_0$, such that $\bigcup_{i\in I}u_i(|C_i|)$ is dense in $|X|$. Here dense means its closure is all of $|X|$. The morphisms $u_i$ need not be immersions or nonconstant; in particular this assertion includes zero-dimensional $X$.

source.place: Chapter I Lemmas 3.5(b) and 3.6, printed p.18, as used in the proof of Theorem 3.4 on p.19. Smooth normalization of irreducible curves nonsingular at the specified point; in dimension zero take a constant map from the affine line.

proof.text: We prove the assertion for all such pointed $Y$ by strong induction on $d=\dim Y$, a finite nonnegative integer by [lem-sfb-point-tangent-cone-dimension]. If $d=0$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (over $\operatorname{Spec}k$) and [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] make $|Y|$ finite discrete. Irreducibility forces $|Y|=\{p\}$. Take $C=\mathbf A^1_k$, $c=0$ and the constant map through $p$. By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] this is smooth of dimension one. It is separated and finite type by its affine polynomial presentation, and geometrically integral since for every extension $K/k$ its coordinate ring $K[t]$ is a domain. If $d=1$, take $C=Y$, $c=p$, $u=1_Y$.

source.place: Chapter I Lemma 3.6, printed p.18, hyperplane/tangent-cone induction; dimension zero added explicitly as allowed by the item.

proof.text: Let $d\ge2$ and suppose the assertion is proved in every positive dimension less than $d$. Put $E=T_{Y/k,p}$. For each linear hyperplane $H\subset E$, [lem-sfb-smooth-prescribed-tangent-hypersurface] gives a smooth separated geometrically integral $(d-1)$-dimensional $D_H$, locally closed in $Y$ through $p$, with tangent space $H$. Apply the induction hypothesis to this pointed $D_H$ and compose its curve maps with $D_H\to Y$. The resulting images are dense in $|D_H|$. Consequently every closed subset $F\subseteq |Y|$ containing the images of all eligible smooth pointed curve maps contains every $|D_H|$: its inverse image in $D_H$ is closed and contains a dense subset.

source.place: Chapter I Lemma 3.6, printed p.18, hyperplane/tangent-cone induction; dimension zero added explicitly as allowed by the item.

proof.text: Give such an $F$ its reduced closed subscheme structure $Z$ (on each affine chart use the radical ideal of functions vanishing on $F$). It contains $p$. By [lem-sfb-point-tangent-cone-dimension], the closed cone $|C_pZ|\subseteq E$ contains every hyperplane $H$. Since $\dim E=d\ge2$, every vector lies in some hyperplane: extend a nonzero vector to a basis and omit another basis vector, and put zero in any hyperplane. Thus the closed cone contains all $k$-points of $E$. It is all of $E$: a polynomial vanishing on $k^d$ is zero, by induction on the number of variables and the fact that a nonzero polynomial in one variable has finitely many roots; an algebraically closed field is infinite. Hence $C_pZ$ is a closed subscheme of the affine space associated to $E$ with the same underlying space; choosing a basis of $E^*$, that coordinate ring is the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, so $\dim C_pZ=\dim k[x_1,\ldots,x_d]=d$ by [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] (a field is Noetherian of dimension $0$). If $F\ne|Y|$, the same cone lemma gives $\dim C_pZ<d$, a contradiction. Therefore $F=|Y|$.

source.place: Chapter I Lemma 3.6, printed p.18, hyperplane/tangent-cone induction; dimension zero added explicitly as allowed by the item.

proof.text: For $d\le1$ step 1 already gives a single curve with dense image. For $d\ge2$, to obtain a set-indexed family, let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal P(|Y|)$ be the set of subsets that occur as images of eligible smooth pointed curve maps. It is a set, being a subcollection of the power set of $|Y|$. The closure of $\bigcup\mathcal S$ contains every such image, so steps 2--3 show it is $|Y|$. For every nonempty open $U\subseteq|Y|$, choose one such curve map whose image meets $U$; such a map exists since otherwise the proper closed subset $|Y|\setminus U$ would contain all images. Index these choices by the set of nonempty opens. Their union meets every nonempty open and is therefore dense. All chosen curves and points satisfy the required hypotheses by their eligibility. This completes the induction and, with $Y=X$ and $p=x_0$, the proof.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q68-b1ccc5a57 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Milne AV I.3.6 (printed p.18, pdf p.24). The split follows its hyperplane/tangent-cone induction, except that it shrinks each hypersurface V_H to a smooth germ instead of normalizing. That is valid because the item allows arbitrary pointed maps. The item statement is unchanged.

Steps 1, 2 and 4 are checked and correct. Step 1 handles d=0 (Noetherian, finite discrete, constant map from A^1, a curve per def-sc-curves) and d=1 (the identity map). Step 2 applies the induction to D_H with every hypothesis present. Step 4 is an elementary set-indexing argument.

Step 3 needs dim A^d_k = d to reach the contradiction dim C_pZ < d, which is not elementary (C1). FIX: cite the Mathlib leaf lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension, which is in sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation, a unit the item's unit uses. I added it to the step's uses and to proof_deps. I also added a clarifying d<=1 sentence at the start of step 4.

Both new nodes are true, statement-only and self-contained, and neither restates the item. lem-sfb-smooth-prescribed-tangent-hypersurface: lift a cotangent form to f; O/f is regular of dimension d-1, hence smooth at the k-point; take the smooth irreducible open piece. Checked on A^2. lem-sfb-point-tangent-cone-dimension: gr O_{Y,p} = Sym E^*, gr of a quotient is a degreewise surjection, dim gr = dim R (00KQ/00P6), proper closed subsets have smaller dimension, and a reduced D lies inside Z. Edge cases Z={p}, Z=Y, the cusp and d=0 hold. Neither duplicates lem-zl-prescribed-point-smooth-member, lem-sfb-regular-hypersurface-initial-form or lem-per-associated-graded-local-dimension.

The three tool_uses (only in the d=0 case) are accepted. No cycle, no SGA. For the maintainer: the existing node lem-sfb-integral-variety-smooth-curve-interpolation (Q77, with no cycle) would also give the item almost directly. That is not a fault, so I dropped no nodes.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
